items.english: Zenpei paid it no mind at all, gazing at the ceiling with a beaming smile. "Ah, Tsunao is a truly splendid fellow."

"Again, again. Father, really." Mitsuyo rose to her feet and with a sudden backhand snatched the air pillow away, so that Zenpei's head dropped with a thump. "Oh, what a cruel thing to do," he said, wincing into a smile. "Serves you right!" Having seized it for good, Mitsuyo pulled out the stopper and with both hands had already squashed it half flat.
notes: The Japanese here says only pillow, but it is the air pillow brought in two paragraphs before; the stopper would otherwise make no sense, so the English names it.

items.english: Left with no choice, Zenpei sat up. "Then shall I make tea to make peace? Bring out those dried sweets we brought." "I know nothing about that," Mitsuyo said, still ruffled, rising with the folded pillow in her arms. "I think I shall go to the bath." "Do not say that. Come, bring them out," he coaxed from below, whereupon, seizing her moment to strike a pose, she drew herself up haughtily. "I am going to the bath. Ask Okumura-san to bring them out for you."

"Out for a walk?" It was Tatsuya, calling from behind. Mitsuyo started and looked back, and finding no way to slip off made her greeting prettily enough. "Is it not a fine view? Have you been down toward the lake yet?" he asked. "No, not yet. I have only just left the inn," she answered self-consciously, the words not coming smoothly and her face bowing of itself. "Then come with me and let us walk a little about. My spirits are clear today, and it is just the weather ordered for a stroll. Your father went out somewhere a while ago, did he not?" in his usual light tone.
notes: The speakers are left to inference in the Japanese; the English assigns the questions about the view and the lake to Tatsuya and the self-conscious answer to Mitsuyo, as the scene requires.
